newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer, watches palladium.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer, watches palladium.

text.p: Gold prices were firmer on Wednesday morning but ironically it was a sharply lower palladium price which was seen as key to market direction, dealers said.

"There could be some surprises from palladium," one dealer said after palladium was fixed at $154.75 per ounce, down from Tuesday afternoon's fresh 20-month high of $157.50, which had effectively carried the precious metals complex higher.
Gold was fixed at $353.15, up from $351.95 previously.
Dealers said New York ended firmer on Tuesday, based on late fund buying in a thin market.
Buying from Swiss banks and short covering in Tokyo and Hong Kong respectively kept gold firm ahead of the London opening.
Initial buying in Europe took gold to its high of $354.55 before selling came in before the fixing.
"Gold still has the ability to surprise. It is volatile in a narrow range," one dealer said.
The current range seemed to be limited to $351.50-$355.00 as dealers saw producer sell orders ready to hit the market as soon as it reached the higher end.
They also said gold's upside was limited by the lack of incentive for speculators to come into the market.
Rampant paper markets and a still very firm dollar were cited as viable alternative attractions for floating investors.
One dealer went as far as to say a return to February's 3-3/4 year low of $336.90 was not impossible.

"There is no fundamental change and no new information available since it saw its low," he said, adding that a market near its low tends to move a lot more sluggishly than gold has over the past few weeks.
Silver was quiet and marked up three cents from Tuesday to $5.24/$5.24 as it consolidated after recent sharp swings.
Palladium prices leapt to recent highs in New York on the back of one bank buying a position, dealers said. It was limit up in Tokyo before profit-taking took prices down by the European opening.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin's cabinet clear-out suggested there was sometime to go before the appointees were in place to begin export negotiations with Japan, dealers said.
Exports have been on ice since the previous export contract ended in December. Palladium was at $155.00/$156.00, down $2.50, and platinum was $0.75 firmer at $383.75/$383.75.
